1999-05-07: Pakistani authorities detain journalist Najam Sethi amid efforts to block a BBC programme on corruption allegations against Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and his family's financial empire.
1999-10-12: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif was dismissed by the military and appeared to be under house arrest following a coup led by General Pervez Musharraf.
1999-11-11: Treason proceedings were launched against Nawaz Sharif and seven others by Pakistan's military-led regime, with accusations including treason and kidnapping that can carry the death penalty.
1999-11-17: Ousted prime minister Nawaz Sharif was flown in secret to Karachi in preparation for a court appearance as Pakistan's military regime detained up to 450 people in a corruption sweep.
1999-11-19: Deposed Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif appeared in public for the first time since the coup, at a special anti-terrorist court in Karachi, where he was remanded in custody pending further investigation.
1999-11-21: Militant supporters of deposed Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif claimed responsibility for a bomb in Lahore that killed six people and injured 18, saying it was to protest against the hijacking of Sharif's government.
1999-11-24: One of Nawaz Sharif's co-accused, Aminuddin Chaudhry, agreed to testify against him in his hijacking and treason case.
1999-12-07: Deposed Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif appeared before the supreme court to face accusations that he was responsible for a 1997 attack on the court.
2000-01-19: Nawaz Sharif's trial on hijacking and conspiracy to murder charges is due to start a week later, following his indictment with his brother and five others.
2000-01-26: The trial of former Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif opened on hijacking, kidnapping, attempted murder, and terrorism charges, hours after the chief justice and five other senior judges left their posts rather than take an oath banning them from challenging military ruler General Pervez Musharraf's decisions.
2000-02-25: A judge is to rule today on whether Pakistan's deposed prime minister Nawaz Sharif should be allowed to testify in open court in his trial on charges including hijacking, kidnapping, attempted murder and terrorism.
2000-02-27: Two leading lawyers for Nawaz Sharif withdrew from his trial after the judge decided to consider imposing a reporting ban on Sharif's evidence.
2000-03-06: Deposed Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif is set to appear before a Karachi court on hijacking and terrorism charges without his top defence lawyer, facing new corruption accusations.
2000-03-17: Two cases are registered against deposed former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, who is on trial in Karachi on charges of attempted murder and hijacking, with at least 16 more cases ready to be filed.
2000-03-31: Kulsoom Sharif, wife of deposed Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif, threatened to defy the military regime and bring protesters onto the streets if her husband is convicted in his hijacking trial.
2000-04-06: A Pakistani anti-terrorism court convicted deposed prime minister Nawaz Sharif of hijacking and terrorism and sentenced him to life imprisonment, while acquitting his brother Shahbaz and five former officials.
2000-04-10: Jailed former Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif is to be interrogated this week over claims he stole hundreds of millions of pounds during his time in power and deposited much of the money in offshore accounts based in Britain.
2000-07-09: Police detain Kulsoom Sharif, wife of jailed former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, for 10 hours and surround her Lahore home to prevent her leading an anti-government rally, arresting at least 200 Pakistan Muslim League members.
2000-07-22: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif was sentenced to 14 years of rigorous imprisonment and banned from holding public office for 21 years after being convicted of failing to pay tax on a helicopter in the first of several corruption trials.
2000-11-28: Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party is in disarray, with Sharif serving a life sentence for hijacking and 14 years for corruption, while his wife Kulsoom has taken charge and led the party into an alliance with the rival Pakistan People's Party, prompting dissident party members to storm the party's Islamabad headquarters and burn pictures of Sharif.
2000-12-10: Deposed Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif was released from prison by the military regime and flew to Saudi Arabia, beginning a new life in exile.
2002-08-05: Former Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif declined to stand in the leadership ballot of his Pakistan Muslim League party, nominating his younger brother Shahbaz Sharif, who was elected unopposed.
2004-05-11: Shahbaz Sharif, brother of exiled former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, was deported to Saudi Arabia hours after arriving in Pakistan, prompting protests in Lahore.
2007-08-22: Pakistan's supreme court ruled that former prime minister Nawaz Sharif is free to return home after seven years in exile.
2007-08-23: Pakistan's Supreme Court ruled that former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has an inalienable right to return from seven-year exile, and Sharif said he planned to return to Pakistan fairly soon.
2007-08-30: A letter warns that in the absence of Benazir Bhutto, the return of Nawaz Sharif, who is associated with fundamentalist Islamist legislation, could skew Pakistan's political balance in favor of Islamists.
Exiled former Pakistani prime minister Nawaz Sharif said he would return to Pakistan on September 10 to fight upcoming parliamentary elections against President Pervez Musharraf.
2007-09-08: Nawaz Sharif left London to return to Pakistan, ending seven years of exile and risking arrest or deportation upon arrival in Islamabad.
2007-09-10: Nawaz Sharif's lawyers filed a petition with Pakistan's supreme court challenging his deportation to Saudi Arabia, arguing that government security agents acted illegally.
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif returned to Pakistan but was swiftly deported to Saudi Arabia after a brief four-hour stay.
2007-09-11: Lawyers for Nawaz Sharif file a petition in Pakistan's supreme court challenging his deportation to Saudi Arabia.
2007-11-25: Nawaz Sharif returns to Pakistan after seven years in exile, landing in Lahore to a chaotic welcome and vowing to challenge President Pervez Musharraf.
2007-11-29: Nawaz Sharif, after returning from exile, said his party would boycott the January 8 election unless sacked judges were restored, and his opposition alliance threatened to boycott elections after Musharraf promised to lift emergency rule.
2007-12-03: Former prime ministers Benazir Bhutto and Nawaz Sharif met in Islamabad and threatened to boycott the January 8 elections unless their demands are met.
Pakistan's electoral commission rejected Nawaz Sharif's application to take part in January's elections on account of his criminal record.
2007-12-10: Nawaz Sharif began campaigning for his Muslim League-N party ahead of the expected January general election, despite being barred from standing due to criminal convictions.
2007-12-31: Nawaz Sharif calls for Pakistan's parliamentary elections to proceed as scheduled on January 8 despite Benazir Bhutto's assassination, while the election committee advises the government to delay them.
2008-01-02: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal describes former Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif as "a force for stability" and "a man who can speak across party lines even to religious extremists" during a meeting with the US Ambassador in Riyadh.
2008-02-18: Nawaz Sharif's opposition party, the Pakistan Muslim League-N, is contesting Pakistan's general election.
2008-02-19: Pakistan People's party says it will seek a national government that includes supporters of Nawaz Sharif after parliamentary elections.
2008-04-16: Nawaz Sharif, back from exile and leading his party in Pakistan's coalition government, is working to sideline President Pervez Musharraf and eventually force him out.
2008-04-29: Nawaz Sharif and Asif Ali Zardari held crisis talks in Dubai to try to avoid a coalition split over reinstating judges deposed by President Pervez Musharraf, but the talks had not yet yielded a breakthrough.
2008-04-30: Nawaz Sharif and Asif Ali Zardari held crisis talks in Dubai over reinstating judges deposed by President Pervez Musharraf, with no breakthrough yet reported.
2008-05-11: Nawaz Sharif withdrew his ministers from Pakistan's coalition government after talks with Asif Ali Zardari collapsed over how to reinstate judges sacked by President Pervez Musharraf.
2008-08-07: Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-N and the Pakistan People's Party agree on a deal to pursue the potential impeachment of President Pervez Musharraf, with Sharif pushing hard for impeachment and seen as the likely political winner.
2008-08-21: Nawaz Sharif's Muslim League-N threatens to leave Pakistan's ruling coalition unless a decision is taken by the next day to reinstate supreme court judges dismissed by former president Pervez Musharraf.
2008-08-24: Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-N announced it was withdrawing from Pakistan's ruling coalition and joining the opposition, blaming the Pakistan People's Party for failing to reinstate judges and for disagreements over Musharraf's successor.
2008-09-02: Pakistani prosecutors said they would press ahead with corruption charges against former prime minister Nawaz Sharif.
2009-02-25: Pakistan's Supreme Court disqualified opposition leader Nawaz Sharif from holding office, provoking a political crisis and angry demonstrations in Punjab province.
2009-03-09: Nawaz Sharif and his opposition party join anti-government lawyers in a "long march" protest convoy due to culminate in a sit-in outside parliament in Islamabad.
2009-03-11: Nawaz Sharif claims he has received credible information from his sources that high-ranking government officials are plotting to kill him, while the government dismisses the allegation as political mileage.
The Pakistani government issued orders to place opposition leader Nawaz Sharif under house arrest ahead of planned protests against the ruling administration.
2009-03-15: The Pakistani government said it would seek a review of a Supreme Court ruling that barred opposition leader Nawaz Sharif and his brother from elected office.
Nawaz Sharif's convoy of opposition "long march" protesters clashed with police in Lahore before he set off for Islamabad, after a claimed house arrest that the government denied.
2009-05-02: The Obama administration is reportedly reaching out to Pakistan's opposition leader Nawaz Sharif amid the country's worsening security crisis, though the push is believed to fall short of a full-scale attempt to broker a power-sharing deal with Asif Ali Zardari.
2009-05-26: Pakistan's Supreme Court lifted an election ban on opposition leader Nawaz Sharif, removing the last hurdle preventing his return to parliament.
2010-01-31: Nawaz Sharif confirmed during a meeting with the US Ambassador that he was ready to work with the Pakistan People's Party in a post-election coalition government, describing the union as "the best thing that could happen in Pakistan."
2010-03-12: Nawaz Sharif refused to budge on demands to reverse the court decision disqualifying the Sharifs, end governor's rule in Punjab, and reinstate the former Chief Justice, despite pressure to delay the lawyers' march.
2013-03-16: Nawaz Sharif's general election campaign kicked off with the dissolution of parliament, as he positioned himself as the frontrunner to become Pakistan's next prime minister.
2013-05-11: Nawaz Sharif's party, the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz, won enough seats in Pakistan's general election to govern without a major coalition deal, setting him up to become prime minister.
2013-05-12: Nawaz Sharif's Muslim League claims victory in Pakistan's election.
2013-05-13: Nawaz Sharif returns to power after Pakistan's general election, with his party poised to form the next government.
2014-01-29: Nawaz Sharif announced he was giving peace talks with the Taliban one last chance by forming a commission of intermediaries to try to talk to the TTP.
2014-05-21: Narendra Modi, India's prime minister-elect, invited Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to his inauguration in Delhi, a gesture that would be the first of its kind if Sharif attends.
2014-08-10: Nawaz Sharif faces planned anti-government protests in Islamabad led by Imran Khan and cleric Tahir-ul-Qadri, with Khan vowing to bring the capital to a standstill on Thursday, Pakistan's independence day, until the government steps down and fresh elections are called.
2014-08-15: A protest convoy led by Imran Khan, demanding the ouster of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government, was pelted with stones by ruling party activists in Gujranwala as it headed toward Islamabad.
2014-08-18: Politicians from Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party announced they will quit their seats in Pakistan's parliament as part of an effort to bring down the government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
2014-08-19: Tens of thousands of anti-government protesters in Islamabad moved toward Pakistan's parliament "red zone," demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government.
2014-08-31: Pakistan's army instructs the embattled government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to resolve the political crisis without violence following clashes between police and protesters demanding his resignation.
2014-09-02: Senior politicians in Pakistan's parliament rallied to defend Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif against protesters demanding his resignation.
2016-10-28: Imran Khan supporters clash with police in Islamabad and Rawalpindi during protests over alleged corruption by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, ahead of a planned November 2 protest.
2016-11-01: Pakistan's Supreme Court agrees to Imran Khan's petition to launch an inquiry into corruption allegations against Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, leading Khan to abandon his planned Islamabad lockdown protest.
2016-11-26: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif names Lieutenant General Qamar Javed Bajwa as the next chief of army staff, to take over from outgoing Raheel Sharif at a change-of-command ceremony on 2016-11-29.
2017-07-28: Pakistan's Supreme Court disqualified Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif from office over undeclared offshore assets linked to his family revealed in the Panama Papers, and he stood down at once.
